spec_match.rationale: Creates real lanes via createWritable({sendOrder}) where supported, writes real BufferSource datagrams (legal while connecting per spec 4.3's note), reads the real maxDatagramSize, and promotes via the mutable sendOrder attribute with read-back.

interactive.rationale: Open/teardown, two text inputs with per-lane queue buttons, and a promote button; every readout (API in use, maxDatagramSize, connection state, queues) reflects real object state.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises two lanes with real options, mid-flight promotion, queued writes, and an honest legacy-door fallback; the page delivers each.

edge_cases.rationale: Pre-155 builds get the real legacy single-queue path (labelled as the limitation the feature removes), no-surface builds get an explicit none state, and the connection-failure transition is narrated when closed rejects.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus, the datagram-writable section, and the sendOrder definition.

conformance.rationale: The suite's defaults, round-trip + mutation, and independent-writables assertions pin this page's lane mechanics; the wire drain order is an honest manual assertion. 2 pass / 7 fail / 1 blocked on Chromium 141.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): open + three queue writes driven on desktop 1280×900 and two on mobile 360×740 — real writes accepted into the legacy shared queue, failure state narrated, overflowX 0, zero failed requests. Partial: the two-lane and promotion paths need a 155+/flagged build.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts lane opening, each write outcome, and promotion read-back; write promises are claimed so the dead session cannot surface unhandled rejections.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; lane badges are black-on-ivory; disabled buttons keep the dark/ivory pair at reduced opacity; inputs are bordered paper surfaces.

accessibility.rationale: Text inputs sit inside visible labels, queues are aria-live polite per lane, buttons are native with 44px height, and the API-in-use line states the mode in text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Driven at both classes with 0px horizontal overflow; the lane grid stacks at 360px; both screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the two-lane path on 155+
openQuestions.detail: On a Chrome 155+/flagged build, confirm the lanes open as separate WebTransportDatagramsWritable objects (sendOrder 10/1 badges), queued writes stay per-lane, and the promote button's assignment reads back 20 — then, when any HTTP/3 endpoint exists, observe actual drain order between lanes.

guidanceConsulted.query: form text inputs with visible labels touch targets mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Visible labels (not placeholders) bound to inputs; 44px targets; box-sizing so full-width inputs don't overflow.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each message input is wrapped in its visible label with min-height 44px and box-sizing:border-box; buttons are 44px native.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive two-panel lane layout stacking on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: auto-fit minmax grids for paired panels so they stack on narrow screens.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The lanes use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px,1fr)); verified stacked at 360px with 0px overflow.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status readout for async API probe result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Polite regions with meaningful text; avoid announcement spam.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The status output and per-lane queue readouts are polite regions updated once per user action, never on timers.

summary: Two-lane datagram scheduler with real creation, options, mutation, and queued writes — degrading to the real legacy single queue on pre-155 builds with the limitation named. Verified with the repo headless-Chromium CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment) on Chromium 141: legacy path exercised with real writes, clean console/network, 0px overflow both classes.
